STAFF'S EIGHTH SET OF DATA REQUESTS TO
GEORGIA POWER COMPANY
	
	Jeremiah Haswell
	Director, Regulatory Affairs
	Georgia Power Company
	Regulatory Affairs Bin 10230
	241 Ralph McGill Blvd., N.E.
	Atlanta, Georgia 30308-3374

	COMES NOW the Staff of the Georgia Public Service Commission (“Commission”) and, pursuant to the authority vested in it by the Commission pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 46-2-57, herein propounds the following interrogatories and requests for production of documents (collectively, “data requests”), to be answered under oath by designated representatives or agents of Georgia Power Company.  Staff requests that a complete set of the responses and supporting documents be filed with the Commission’s Executive Secretary in the manner set forth in Utility Rule 515-2-.04(4).  Staff requests that an original and five (5) copies be filed with the Executive Secretary of the Commission.  Accompanied therewith shall be an electronic version of the filing, which shall be made on a 3 ½ inch diskette or a CD ROM containing an electronic version of its filing in Microsoft Word® for text documents or Excel® for spreadsheets.  As contemplated by law, responses to these Data Requests are expected from Georgia Power Company on or before October 16, 2026. 


DEFINITIONS

As may be used in this document:  
1.	“The Company,” “Georgia Power” or “The Utility” means Georgia Power Company and its present and former officers, employees, agents, representatives, directors, and all other persons acting or purporting to act on behalf of said Company.
The term “you” and “your” refer to “the Company.”
The term “person” means any natural person, corporation, corporate division, partnership, other unincorporated association, trust, government agency, or entity.
The term “document” or “documentation” shall have the broadest possible meaning under applicable law.  “Document” or “documentation” means every writing or record of every type and description that is in the possession, custody or control of the Company including, but not limited to, correspondence, memoranda, e-mails, drafts, workpapers, summaries, stenographic or handwritten notes, studies, notices, publications, books, pamphlets, reports, surveys, minutes or statistical compilations, computer and other electronic records or tapes or printouts, including, but not limited to, electronic mail files; and copies of such writing or records containing any commentary or notation whatsoever that does not appear in the original.  The term “document” or “documentation” further includes, by way of illustration and not limitation, schedules, progress schedules, time logs, drawings, computer disks, chart projections, time tables, summaries of other documents, minutes, surveys, work sheets, drawings, comparisons, evaluations, laboratory and testing reports, telephone call records, personal diaries, calendars, personal notebooks, personal reading files, transcripts, witness statements and indices.
The term “referring or relating to” means consisting of, containing, mentioning, suggesting, reflecting, concerning, regarding, summarizing, analyzing, discussing, involving, dealing with, emanating from, directed at, pertaining to in any way, or in any way logically or factually connected or associated with the matter discussed.
“And” and “or” as used herein shall be construed both conjunctively and disjunctively and each shall include the other whenever such construction will serve to bring within the scope of these discovery requests any information that would not otherwise be brought within their scope.
The singular as used herein shall include the plural and the masculine gender shall include the feminine and the neuter.
“Identify” or “identifying” or “identification” when used in reference to a person other than a natural person means to state:  the full name of the person and any names under which it conducts business; the present or last known address of the person; and, the present or last known telephone number of the person.
“Identify” or “identifying” or “identification” when used in reference to a document means to provide with respect to each document requested to be identified by these discovery requests a description of the document that is sufficient for purposes of a request to produce or a subpoena duces tecum, including the following:						
the type of document (e.g., letter, memorandum, etc.);
the date of the document; the title or label of the document;
the Bates number or other identifier used to number the document for use in  litigation; the identity of the originator;
the identity of each person to whom it was sent;
the identity of each person to whom a copy or copies were sent;
a summary of the contents of the document;
the name and last known address of each person who presently has possession, custody or control of the document;
if any such document was, but is no longer, in your possession,  custody or control or is no longer in existence, state whether it: (1) is missing or lost; (2) has been destroyed; or (3) has been transferred voluntarily or involuntarily, and if so, state the circumstances surrounding the authorization for each such disposition and the date of such disposition.					
“Identify”, “identifying” or identity” when used in reference to a communication should be read to include information regarding the date of the communication, whether the communication was written or oral, the identity of all parties and witnesses to the communication, the substance of what was said and/or transpired and, if written, the identity of the document(s) containing or referring to the communication.


INSTRUCTIONS
If you contend that any response to any data request may be withheld under the attorney-client privilege, the attorney work product doctrine or any other privilege or basis, please state the following with respect to each such response in order to explain the basis for the claim of privilege and to permit adjudication of the propriety of that claim:	
the privilege asserted and its basis.
the nature of the information withheld;
the subject matter of the document, except to the extent that you claim it is privileged.
The answers provided should first restate the question asked and also provide the name of the Company employee(s) or agents responsible for compiling and providing the information contained in each answer. 
These data requests are to be answered with reference to all information in your possession, custody or control or reasonably available to you.  These discovery requests are intended to include requests for information, which is physically within your possession, custody or control as well as in the possession, custody or control of your agents, attorneys, or other third parties from which such documents may be obtained.
If any data request cannot be responded to or answered in full, answer to the extent possible and specify the reasons for your inability to answer fully.
These data requests are continuing in nature and require supplemental responses should information unknown to you at the time you serve your responses to these interrogatories subsequently become known.
 If you contend that any response to any data request may be withheld under the attorney-client privilege, the attorney work product doctrine or any other privilege or basis, please state the following with respect to each such response in order to explain the basis for the claim of privilege and to permit adjudication of the propriety of that claim:  
the privilege asserted and its basis.
a log should be provided identifying starting and ending bates numbers.
the nature of the information withheld;
the subject matter of the document, except to the extent that you claim it is privileged.
a description of the document to which the privilege applies. 


PUBLIC DISCLOSURE
Ten-Tear Transmission Plan


There are several projects that did not carry over from the 2022 Ten-Year Plan (TYP) into the 2025 TYP. These projects are not on the cancelled project list provided in the 2025 TYP. The following projects have ISDs beyond 2025 and are not included in the 2025 TYP: 19611, 20005, 18492, 19997, 19991, 20067, 19623, 20000, 19599, 20019, 20020, 14222, 19628, 20003, 12063, 15228, 20004, 19187, 17993. Please provide reports or documentation that describe the status of each of those projects. 
Please identify all projects that were completed between the release of the 2022 TYP and the 2025 TYP. Please provide the project identification number, date of project completion, project cost, and any modifications between the project scope detailed in the 2022 TYP and the final project design.
Please provide all procedure documents, planning manuals, processes, and all other material on how Georgia Power's transmission planning team conducts the Ten-Year Plan process. This includes assumptions based on powerflow analyses, load forecasting, and other location-based considerations around transmission planning infrastructure.
From the 2025 IRP Main Document 11.3 Strategic Transmission, “A key component of an IRP is the ability to consider impacts to the transmission system when making generating resource decisions.” Explain the separate  transmission evaluations being made now. Does it also include large loads as well as generation?  
Please provide planning reports or any other documentation that best describes project progress from 2022 to present
Other than the semiannual board meetings, please provide any outgoing material on project statuses and progress given to the stakeholders through meetings, email, etc. This can include memos, PowerPoint slides, and graphics. 


Please provide all semiannual board meeting presentation slides from 2022 to present. Some examples include board meetings materials, briefings etc. that best describe the detailed project status. 
Cancellations have grown in both count and dollar value between the 2022 and 2025 Ten-Year Plans. The 2022 TYP listed 9 cancelled projects, page 16, totaling roughly xxxxxxx. The 2025 TYP listed 30 cancelled projects, pages 23-25, totaling roughly xxxxxxx. 
Please provide a narrative explanation for why project cancellations have increased.
For each cancellation listed in the 2022 TYP, please describe the reason(s) and provide all related studies or documentation supporting the cancellation. 
For each cancellation listed in the 2025 TYP, please describe the reason(s) and provide all related studies or documentation supporting the cancellation. If the cancelled project will be replaced by another project, provide the related studies or documentation.
Please identify any projects that were cancelled due to a change in status (e.g. cancellation or delay) of a proposed large load project. If the cancelled project will be replaced by another project, provide the related studies or documentation.
Of the xxxxxxxxxx in the 2025 plan (per page 23 of the 2025 TYP), roughly xxxxxxxxxxxx is attributable to 216 projects that were not present in the 2022 plan at all. Please identify which of these new projects are driven, in whole or in part, by large load interconnection requests.
Several of the largest new projects are 500kV lines (e.g., Hatch-Wadley 500kV, Ashley Park-Wansley 500kV, Cavender Drive-Wansley 500kV). For each of these projects, what specific load or generation initiated the need, and when was each first identified as necessary?



Of the 107 projects in the 2022 plan, only 39 still appear as the same TEAMS numbered project in the 2025 plan. 
Please confirm whether TEAMS numbers are ever reused or reassigned to a different project scope, and if so, provide the protocol for how that is tracked and disclosed.
If any of the projects from the 2022 TYP are listed under different TEAMS numbers in the 2025 TYP, please provide a reconciliation of the project numbering.
If a project scope changes in any way, will the TEAMS number be maintained? What would cause a project’s TEAMS number to change? 
For the projects that persist across both the 2022 TYP and 2025 TYP, cost estimates increased by more than xxxxx for many of them, including projects with the following TEAMS numbers: 18832, 18679, 19610, 18960, 20015, 19632, 19601, 19996, 19992, 20002, 18668. For each of these, please provide the historical cost estimate data and a brief narrative explanation for what specifically changed (e.g., scope, contingency, materials, etc.).
In the 2022 TYP, Table 5, the load forecast contains no "Large Load" forecast category. The version of Table 5 in the 2025 TYP introduces a new "Large Load Forecast" column for each entity, separate from the general coincidence forecast. Please explain in what year this methodology was officially implemented and were there large loads embedded into the 2022 vintage?
Across the 2025 TYP plan, most projects' "Supporting Statement" is phrased purely in electrical criteria terms (i.e., thermal overloads, voltage violations, contingency violations, etc.) with no reference to the specific load or customer driving the need. For projects being driven in whole or in part due to incremental large loads, please provide a supplemental supporting statement with the specific load or generation driver.




Georgia Power's TYP project listings reference zone numbers in addition to TEAMS numbers (e.g., in project location or planning area designations.
Please describe the zone numbering methodology, including how zone boundaries are determined, how zone numbers are assigned to projects, and whether zone numbers or boundaries have changed between the 2022 TYP and 2025 TYP.
Please provide a supporting map showing all current transmission planning zones, their boundaries, and zone numbers.
